r01_00.why: Undifferentiated two-tone dither across the entire field with a green speckle strip at the bottom — no course, no joint, no edge, nothing a wall is made of.

r01_01.why: Perfectly ruled 1px mortar lines at fixed intervals with a pale cream strip on the bottom row that tiles into an unbroken banner across the whole map every 32 pixels; no top surface, no thickness, no repair anywhere.

r01_02.why: A flat green-grey field partitioned by uniform 1px dark lines — reads as a printed maze or circuit trace, not stone, with zero thickness and no top band at all.

r01_03.why: A hard-outlined black niche with two panels sits centred on a masonry background and tiles into a polka-dot grid of identical windows.

r01_04.why: Five rows of blockwork sit on top of two-thirds of a tile that is checkerboard dither and scattered black pixels with no structure under it.

r01_05.why: Wall-to-wall pale-green static with a solid stripe at the base — no discernible element of any kind.

r01_06.why: Flat horizontal banding with saturated mint lines that read as painted glow and a lone orange blob that tiles into a regular polka-dot; this is shelving or ductwork seen flat-on, not a wall face with a top.

r01_07.why: The upper two-thirds is structureless dark mottle and the lower third is a flat saturated green slab, giving a baked top-dark/bottom-light value ramp across the tile.

r01_08.why: A dark 1px border runs down both inset edges and along top and bottom, so it tiles into a visible grid of framed panels rather than continuous surface.

r01_09.why: Single-value flat blocks separated by 1px pen lines, with a wide empty band at the base carrying a repeating row of little arch glyphs that reads as a decorative frieze.

flip_list: The pale bottom strip in r01_01, r01_05, r01_07 and r01_09 tiles into a continuous horizontal banner every 32px. Delete it, and instead put the top-surface band along the TOP edge, 4–6px deep, in the same stone family as the face but a distinct value step, with the join between top and face broken irregularly rather than ruled straight — so vertical tiling reads as one wall with one cap, not as striped courses.

The mortar joints in r01_01, r01_02 and r01_09 are uniform 1px dark lines. Vary them: 1px where beds are tight, 2–3px where the bed has crumbled out, and let three or four joints be filled with a lighter packing material. Break at least two joints so a block's edge is chipped back and the joint runs into the block face.

The blocks in r01_02 and r01_09 are flat single-colour fills. Give each block interior a two- to three-value break with the darker values pooled at the lower edge of the block where dust collects — not a bevel, not a highlight, just uneven stone that reads as quarried rather than filled.

r01_00, r01_04, r01_05 and r01_07 have no load path. Draw the actual structure first: coursed blocks or a stacked rubble face with visible course lines, then dither only inside the block faces at a maximum of two adjacent palette values, never as the whole tile.

Nothing in the set shows a repair. Add the orc work: a salvaged timber baulk laid horizontally across two or three courses with visible thickness (a 2px darker edge along its underside where it stands proud of the stone, not a painted stripe), and a driven iron pin with a visible head at each end, each pin sitting in a hole that has spalled the stone around it.
r01_03: remove the black-outlined niche entirely. If a recess is wanted, it must be authored as a separate tile, not as the repeating surface.

r01_08: delete the dark border columns at x=1 and x=30 and the bright row at y=31, and let the block courses run off all four edges mid-block so neighbouring copies interlock instead of butting into a frame.

r01_06: drop the mint (124,185,168 / 149,201,176) and the orange blob — they sit outside the cold palette and read as emissive. If a wet or salt-crusted line is wanted, keep it within two steps of the surrounding stone hue and break it so it does not run edge to edge.
Every survivor must be checked as a 3x3 tile before submission: any element that produces a continuous line or a regularly-spaced motif at the 32px pitch is disqualifying.
